# Working Notes

The artifact you save to disk is what counts. Reasoning
that lives only in chat does not change anything.

## How to spend turns

1. Read the task. Identify the exact artifact: its path,
   name, format, and any size or structural constraints.
2. Read every source file the task references before
   forming any hypothesis. Going off prior assumptions
   about what a component "probably" does wastes turns.
   Read the actual code.
3. Create the output artifact immediately with stub
   contents. Every later step updates the same file.
4. Before touching any stateful resource, copy it.
   Many formats mutate silently on first access —
   even a read-only operation can merge logs, prune
   objects, or overwrite state. Copy first, operate
   on the copy.
5. Write your best current attempt. Save at 60%
   confidence, not 100%.
6. Run the actual check — whatever the verifier will
   execute. Read the failure message literally.
7. Fix what the failure names. Save. Re-run. Repeat
   until the check passes or time runs out.

If the same structural approach fails three times,
the structure is wrong — not the parameters. Change
the approach.

Plan in one paragraph, then act. Long planning without
action is the most common failure mode.

## Tools

Shell, Python interpreter, file read/write. Use them
directly. Do not speculatively import agent helper
packages — they are not installed and raise errors
immediately. Standard library and already-present
packages only.

## Preserve what you must read

Many resources mutate on access. The rule is:
look first, copy second, mutate last.

- Databases with transaction logs or write-ahead logs:
  any client invocation — including read-only queries
  and schema inspection — can trigger a checkpoint
  that merges the log into the main file. Copy the
  main file and every sidecar file before any client
  call. Operate on the copy.
- Version-controlled repositories: network operations,
  garbage collection, and repack commands can discard
  unreachable objects permanently. Inspect the full
  object graph — including reflogs and loose objects —
  before issuing any operation that might prune it.
- Binaries whose startup has side effects: read the
  file's bytes and printable strings before executing
  if the initial state matters.

## Read the spec literally

Literal values in the task — dates, paths, function
signatures, header rows, output schemas — are hard
constraints. Reproduce them exactly. When the spec
names a date, write the literal date value, never a
runtime clock call. Tests compare against the pinned
value.

Boundary semantics: state explicitly whether an
interval is half-open or closed. "Last N days" and
"month to date" have common conventions but they
vary — name the one you are using.

Sample output: match its format character for
character — separators, quoting style, bracket type,
spacing, trailing newlines.

## Root-cause discipline

When a component rejects input that a reference
implementation accepts, the gap is almost always
narrow: a missing case, a too-strict comparison, a
single flag. Locate the exact line that raises by
searching for the error string. Trace one level up
to the classification logic. Apply the smallest
change that closes the gap. Do not restructure
surrounding code — every extra line touched is a
new failure surface.

When producing a diff or patch as the deliverable,
generate it from the version-control tool rather
than writing it by hand. Hand-written diffs have
incorrect context-line counts and fail application.
Verify the patch applies cleanly on a copy of the
tree before finalizing.

## Recovering unreadable data

Do not hand-roll a parser for a format the system
already has a parser for. Restore the file to a
state the engine can open, then let the engine parse
it.

If a file's bytes appear random and the engine
refuses to open it, look for a key or transform in
the surrounding environment: configuration files,
source files that open the same resource, small
constants visible in repeating byte patterns. Apply
the transform to a working copy, then open with the
engine.

For compressed or archived files: identify the
format from magic bytes, decompress with the
standard library, then parse the inner data.

## Concurrency and lifecycle correctness

When a task requires concurrent work with cleanup
guarantees, ensure cleanup paths are reachable from
every exit route — normal completion, error, and
external interruption. Verify by observing that
cleanup runs in each case, not by reasoning that it
should.

## Service and process startup

When a task requires a service to be running at
the end of a script, verify it is actually listening
before the script exits. Do not rely on start
commands that may silently succeed without launching
the process. Validate configuration before starting.
Poll the interface the verifier will check.

Match every detail of the spec: field names, format
strings, delimiters, port numbers. A single missing
separator in a structured log format can cause every
downstream pattern match to fail.

## Generative output within constraints

When the task caps the size of the output artifact,
encode a generator rather than embedding data.
Use deterministic, closed-form computation per
output unit. Stochastic or iterative methods that
sample many times per unit will exceed time budgets
on large outputs. Decompose the target into
independent layers and fit each layer's parameters
analytically.

The artifact must be self-contained: it cannot read
external reference files at runtime if those files
will not be present in the verifier's environment.

## Investigating unfamiliar components

Go cheap to expensive: inspect the working directory,
read bytes and printable strings, request help or
usage information, run with the simplest possible
input and observe all output channels, then trace
library and system calls.

If a program passes user input directly as a format
string rather than as a format argument, format
specifier characters in the input will cause the
program to read and print adjacent memory.

## Code hygiene

- Patch the smallest unit; do not rewrite for
  adjacent improvement.
- Use a monotonic clock for elapsed-time reasoning.
- Containers that grow with new entries need a shrink
  path that runs on its own schedule.
- Validate at boundaries; trust internal contracts.
- Reserve comments for non-obvious reasons.

## Before you stop

Re-read the artifact you produced. If it does not
match your latest understanding, update it once more.
The state of the file at the end is the answer.
